name: RBXScriptSignal
simple: RBXScriptSignal is the official name for an event in Roblox, like `Touched`, `PlayerAdded` or `Activated`. An event is something that can happen. You attach a function to it with `:Connect`, and Roblox runs your function every time it happens.
analogy: A signal is like a doorbell. `:Connect` is you saying 'every time the doorbell rings, I will go open the door'. `:Once` is 'I will answer it just the next time'. `:Wait` is standing by the door doing nothing else until it rings.
whenToUse: Any time you want code to run when something happens: a part is touched, a player joins, a button is clicked.
Waiting for something to happen before continuing (`:Wait`).
Running something only the first time an event happens (`:Once`).
where: Signals are found on objects, like `part.Touched` or `Players.PlayerAdded`. Use them with a dot to get the event and a colon to call its method: `part.Touched:Connect(...)`. Works in Scripts and LocalScripts.

terms.event / signal: Something that can happen in the game, like a touch or a click. Roblox 'fires' the event when it happens.
terms.fire: When the event happens and Roblox runs all the connected functions.
terms.connect: Attaching your function to an event so it runs each time the event fires.
terms.connection: The object you get back from `:Connect`. You can keep it and call `:Disconnect()` later to stop listening.
terms.callback / handler: The function you connect to an event. Roblox calls it for you when the event fires.
terms.yield: To pause your script and wait. `:Wait()` pauses until the event fires.
terms.Actor / parallel: An advanced way to run code on several CPU cores at once. Only scripts inside an Actor object can use `ConnectParallel`. Beginners can skip it.

examples.title: Do something when a part is touched
examples.place: Script inside a Part in Workspace
examples.code:
local part = script.Parent

-- Touched is a signal. Connect a function to it.
part.Touched:Connect(function(otherPart)
	print(otherPart.Name .. " touched me!")
end)
explain: Every time something touches the part, Roblox runs the function and tells us what touched it.

examples.title: Connect, Once and Wait side by side
examples.code:
local Players = game:GetService("Players")

-- Runs for EVERY player who joins
Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(function(player)
	print("Welcome, " .. player.Name)
end)

-- Runs only for the FIRST player who joins
Players.PlayerAdded:Once(function(player)
	print(player.Name .. " was the first one here!")
end)

-- Pauses this script until someone joins, then continues
local firstPlayer = Players.PlayerAdded:Wait()
print("Game can start now that " .. firstPlayer.Name .. " is here")
explain: `:Once` listens one time, then stops by itself.
`:Wait` pauses the script and gives back what the event sent.

gotchas: Use a dot to get the event and a colon to use it: `part.Touched:Connect(...)`, not `part:Touched:Connect`.
Connections keep running until you disconnect them or the object is destroyed. Disconnect ones you no longer need to avoid slowdowns.
`:Wait()` stops the whole script until the event fires. If it never fires, the code after it never runs.
Pass a function to `:Connect`, not the result of calling one: `:Connect(onTouch)`, not `:Connect(onTouch())`.

RBXScriptSignal:Connect.simple: Attaches a function to the event. Every time the event fires, your function runs and gets whatever the event passes (like the part that touched). Returns a connection you can disconnect later.
RBXScriptSignal:Connect.example:
-- LocalScript inside a TextButton in StarterGui
local button = script.Parent

local connection = button.Activated:Connect(function()
	print("Button clicked!")
end)

RBXScriptSignal:ConnectParallel.simple: An advanced version of `Connect` that runs your function in parallel (on another CPU core) for speed. Only works in scripts placed inside an Actor. Most games never need it.
RBXScriptSignal:ConnectParallel.example:
-- Script inside an Actor in Workspace
local RunService = game:GetService("RunService")

RunService.Heartbeat:ConnectParallel(function()
	-- heavy math can go here, running in parallel
	local total = 0
	for i = 1, 1000 do
		total += i
	end
end)
RBXScriptSignal:ConnectParallel.gotcha: In parallel mode you cannot change most things in the game. Call `task.synchronize()` before changing parts.

RBXScriptSignal:Once.simple: Like `Connect`, but your function runs only the next time the event fires, then disconnects automatically.
RBXScriptSignal:Once.example:
-- Script in ServerScriptService
local Players = game:GetService("Players")

Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(function(player)
	-- Only greet on their first spawn
	player.CharacterAdded:Once(function(character)
		print(player.Name .. " spawned for the first time")
	end)
end)

RBXScriptSignal:Wait.simple: Pauses your script until the event fires, then gives back what the event sent. Handy for 'wait until X happens'.
RBXScriptSignal:Wait.example:
-- LocalScript in StarterPlayerScripts
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local player = Players.LocalPlayer

-- Use the current character, or wait for one to spawn
local character = player.Character or player.CharacterAdded:Wait()
print("My character is ready:", character.Name)
RBXScriptSignal:Wait.gotcha: If the event never fires, your script waits forever.
